concerns.text: T040 is marked [P] (parallel-safe) but explicitly depends on T015 output ('reading data/results/ast_generation_latency.json'). A task consuming an artifact cannot be parallel-safe with the producer of that artifact. This violates the 'Producer before consumer' rule.

T049b is marked [P] but depends on T049a (baseline generation) and T015 (AST generation). It consumes artifacts produced by other tasks, making it impossible to run in parallel with its producers. The [P] tag is incorrect.

T030 is marked [P] but the description states it 'sequentially calls the adapter generator (T015) and evaluator (T021)'. A task that orchestrates a sequential loop of other tasks is not parallel-safe with those tasks. The [P] tag is misleading.

T021 depends on T055 (Data Acquisition) and T016. T055 is in Phase 7, while T021 is in Phase 4. The task order places the consumer (T021) before the producer (T055) in the phase sequence, violating data-flow dependencies. Phase 7 must complete before Phase 4 tasks can execute.

T032 depends on T031a and T033. T033 generates 'sensitivity_summary.csv' which T032 parses. However, T033 is listed after T032 in the task list, and T032 is marked as depending on T033. While the dependency text is correct, the visual ordering in the list (T032 before T033) is confusing and risks execution errors if a script iterates linearly. Re-order T033 before T032.
